source_evidence.anchor: the notion of the Lp norm of a random variable
source_evidence.observation: For finite p, the source defines the Lp quantity by ||X||_{Lp} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) for p in (0, infinity).

source_evidence.anchor: This definition can be extended to p = infinity
source_evidence.observation: At p = infinity, the source defines ||X||_{L-infinity} as the essential supremum of |X|.

source_evidence.anchor: For fixed p and a given probability space (Omega, Sigma, P), the classical vector space Lp = Lp(Omega, Sigma, P)
source_evidence.observation: The source fixes p and the probability space and introduces Lp(Omega, Sigma, P) as a classical vector space of random variables on Omega.

source_evidence.anchor: consists of all random variables X on Omega with finite Lp norm
source_evidence.observation: The displayed definition is Lp = {X : ||X||_{Lp} < infinity}; thus membership is exactly finiteness of the Lp quantity.

source_evidence.anchor: a random variable X on a probability space (Omega, Sigma, P)
source_evidence.observation: The source describes a random variable as a function X : Omega -> R and expectation as its Lebesgue integral.

contract_plain_english: Fix a positive exponent p, allowing p = infinity, and fix a probability space (Omega, Sigma, P). The space Lp(Omega, Sigma, P) consists exactly of the real-valued random variables X on Omega whose Lp quantity is finite: (E|X|^p)^(1/p) for finite p, or ess sup |X| for p = infinity. This narrowed definition does not itself claim that the quantity is a norm or that the space is Banach or Hilbert. The passage does not say whether random variables are identified when they agree almost surely.
